   This immediately rules out A, C, and E, which do not contain three cubes in a straight row.

3. Thus the dark piece is either B (an L-shape) or D (a T-shape).

4. The cross-hatched piece occupies the visible \(2\times 2\) block in the upper-left. If the dark piece were the T-shape D, its fourth cube would have to be behind the middle of the three visible cubes. That would leave an isolated non-dark cube in the bottom back-left position, so the remaining white piece could not be one connected four-cube shape.

5. Therefore the fourth dark cube must be at one end of the visible row, hidden behind it. This is the L-shaped piece, choice B.
